papers.why: The paper makes gelatin gels with seven different amounts of a bis-oxazoline crosslinker and prints, in the running text, the stiffness and the swelling at each amount; stiffness peaks and swelling bottoms out at a middle amount (1.5 eq) rather than rising or falling steadily.

records.label: TanOxo-Gel (tannic-acid-compacted, bis-oxazoline-crosslinked gelatin): storage modulus G' retained after 5 days in water, versus bis-oxazoline loading

quotes.text: the retained modulus after 5 days increased from 14.7 kPa at 0.5 eq to 27.2 kPa at 0.75 eq, 30.8 kPa at 1.0 eq, and 33.1 kPa at 1.25 eq, before reaching a maximum of 45.6 kPa
before reaching a maximum of 45.6 kPa at 1.5 eq and then decreasing again to 35.6 kPa at 1.75 eq and 28.5 kPa at 2.0 eq.

records.note: Non-monotonic: rises to 1.5 eq then falls. Shear storage modulus from oscillatory rheology. The next paragraph restates three of these as 33.1, 45.6 and 35 kPa at 1.25, 1.5 and 1.75 eq (35 versus 35.6 at 1.75 eq is the paper's own rounding or inconsistency). No unit conversion.

records.label: Oxo-GelPHy (bis-oxazoline-crosslinked gelatin without tannic acid): storage modulus G' retained after 5 days in water, versus bis-oxazoline loading

quotes.text: After 5 days of immersion, the 1.25, 1.5, and 1.75 eq Oxo-GelPHy formulations retained G' values of 4.4, 7.1, and 5.4 kPa, respectively

records.note: Only three doses printed for this control series; non-monotonic (peak at 1.5 eq). Source uses non-breaking hyphens and a prime character, normalised here.

records.label: Oxo-GelPHy (no tannic acid): relative swelling (volume change relative to initial state) after 21 days in water, versus bis-oxazoline loading

quotes.text: At Day 21, the remaining formulations exhibited relative swelling values of 225.0% at 1.0 eq, 185.0% at 1.25 eq, 78.0% at 1.5 eq, 155.0% at 1.75 eq, and 234.6% at 2.0 eq.

records.note: The 0.50 and 0.75 eq gels fell apart by Day 21, so the paper gives no number for them. Non-monotonic: minimum at 1.5 eq.

records.label: TanOxo-Gel: relative volumetric change after 21 days in water (referenced to Day 0), versus bis-oxazoline loading

quotes.text: At Day 21, the 0.50 eq formulation showed a relative volumetric change of 178.0%. Increasing the bis-oxazoline loading to 0.75 and 1.00 eq reduced the expansion to 125.0% and 56.0%, respectively.
quotes.where: Section 2.3, paragraph on Figure 3A right panel

quotes.text: The 1.25 eq formulation showed a relative volumetric change of 24.9%, whereas the 1.50 eq formulation most effectively retained the compacted state, with a relative volumetric change of -31.0%.
At 1.75 and 2.00 eq, the corresponding values were 11.7% and 88.3%, respectively.

records.note: CAVEAT: the 1.5 eq value is negative (-31.0%, the gel stayed smaller than its starting volume), so this series breaks the positive-numbers rule as printed; a volume ratio V/V0 would be positive (e.g. 0.69 at 1.5 eq) but I did not convert. Non-monotonic: minimum at 1.5 eq. The paper prints the minus sign as a Unicode minus.

records.label: TanOxo-Gel: relative volumetric change in the compacted state straight after tannic acid treatment (Shr), versus bis-oxazoline loading

inputs.unit: % relative volumetric change vs Day 0 (negative = shrinkage)

quotes.text: The relative volumetric change at the compacted state (Shr) ranged from -69.0% at 0.50 eq and -67.8% at 0.75 eq to -74.8% at 1.25 eq, reaching a maximum compaction of -77.8% at 1.50 eq.
quotes.where: Section 2.3, paragraph on Figure 3A right panel

records.note: CAVEAT: all values are negative (shrinkage in the tannic acid bath, not swelling in water), so this series does not satisfy the positive-numbers rule and is a weak fit to the law; listed for completeness. Values for 1.0, 1.75 and 2.0 eq are not printed.

records.label: Tan-GelPHy (gelatin soaked in tannic acid, no covalent crosslinker): storage modulus G' after 5 days, versus tannic acid bath concentration

inputs.dose_unit: wt.% tannic acid in the immersion bath

quotes.text: After 5 days, G' increased from 18.9 kPa at 5 wt.% tannic acid to 23.0, 29.3, 31.6, and 32.9 kPa at 10, 20, 30, and 40 wt.%, respectively.

records.note: CAVEAT: tannic acid here is a physical (hydrogen-bonding) crosslinker, not a covalent one, and the dose is the bath concentration, not the amount in the gel. Whether this counts as a crosslinker dose series is a judgement call. Monotonic increase.

candidate_laws.statement: Stiffness and swelling resistance are both best at an intermediate crosslinker loading (1.5 eq) and get worse on either side, which the authors attribute to hydrolysis and one-ended (non-bridging) reactions at high loading.
candidate_laws.quote: Within this screening series, 1.5 eq gave the highest initial and retained modulus, reaching 55.7 kPa initially and remaining at 45.6 kPa after immersion.

papers.why: The preprint makes cellulose-based absorbent gels with different amounts of citric acid or BTCA crosslinker and prints, in two tables and the text, the stiffness and the saline uptake at each amount.

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, citric acid: storage modulus G' at 1 Hz (gel swollen in DI water) versus citric acid loading

quotes.where: Table 2 (rows 0.0% CA, 0.5% CA, 2.0% CA; columns G' (Pa), Mc, Nc, crosslink density, mesh size)

quotes.text: the 2.0% CA sample exhibits the highest G' (949 ± 1 Pa) at 1Hz among the hydrogels crosslinked with Citric Acid

records.note: CAVEAT: the series reaches three doses only by counting the uncrosslinked control (dose 0), which is not a positive number; with positive doses only there are two points. Monotonic increase. Slashes in the table quote mark row breaks.

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, BTCA: storage modulus G' at 1 Hz versus BTCA loading

quotes.text: G' increases with crosslinker content and type, ranging from 21 Pa in the non-crosslinked sample to 187 Pa at 0.5% CA, and up to 3489 Pa at 1.0% BTCA.

records.note: CAVEAT: only two BTCA doses are printed; the third point is the shared uncrosslinked control, which the table labels '0.0% CA' and which is dose 0 (not positive). Weak series; large error bars (±468, ±1400).

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, citric acid: centrifuge retention capacity (CRC) in 0.9% saline versus citric acid loading

quotes.where: Table 1 (columns TCC mmol/g, AUL g/g, CRC g/g)

records.note: CRC is fluid retained after centrifugation, a swelling-capacity measure, not free equilibrium swelling. The uncrosslinked control row (0.0% CA) prints CRC 17 ± 3 g/g; left out of the inputs because dose 0 is not positive. Decreasing over the positive doses.

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, citric acid: absorption under load (AUL, 6.2 kPa) in 0.9% saline versus citric acid loading

quotes.where: Table 1 (columns TCC mmol/g, AUL g/g, CRC g/g)

records.note: AUL is uptake under pressure, so it mixes swelling with gel strength; a loose fit to 'swelling'. The uncrosslinked control row prints AUL 3.6 ± 0.0 g/g (dose 0, left out). Flat then slightly lower.

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, BTCA: centrifuge retention capacity (CRC) in 0.9% saline versus BTCA loading

quotes.where: Table 1 (columns TCC mmol/g, AUL g/g, CRC g/g)

records.note: Retention RISES with BTCA dose here, opposite to the usual direction; the authors attribute it to unreacted carboxyl groups. Uncrosslinked control prints 17 ± 3 g/g (dose 0, left out). The body text describing Figure 2D (CRC dropping from 0.5% then recovering to 15 g/g at 2%) does not obviously match this table.

records.label: CMC-HEC hydrogel, BTCA: absorption under load (AUL, 6.2 kPa) in 0.9% saline versus BTCA loading

quotes.where: Table 1 (columns TCC mmol/g, AUL g/g, CRC g/g)

records.note: AUL is uptake under pressure (mixes swelling with gel strength). Increasing with dose. Uncrosslinked control prints 3.6 ± 0.0 g/g (dose 0, left out).

records.label: CMC-starch hydrogel, BTCA: absorption under load (AUL) in 0.9% saline versus BTCA loading

quotes.text: For BTCA-Starch (Figure 2B), AUL showed similar behavior: from 5.5 g/g at 1% to 6 g/g at 2%, then declining to 3.5 g/g at 9% BTCA.

records.note: Numbers are printed in the text, but they are the authors' own description of a plot (Figure 2B), so they are probably rounded; no table backs them. Non-monotonic. The companion citric acid/starch sentence gives only two values ('7 g/g at 1% CA', 'below 3 g/g at 9%'), so no series there.

candidate_laws.statement: Rubber-elasticity estimate: molar mass between crosslinks, crosslink density and mesh size are computed from the plateau storage modulus G' (with density, gas constant, temperature, Avogadro number), so mesh size shrinks as G' rises (5.8E-08 m at 21 Pa to 1.2E-08 m at 3489 Pa).
candidate_laws.quote: the network parameters can be determined using the rubber elastic plateau G', the density ρ, the gas constant R, the temperature T, and the Avogadro number NA.

candidate_laws.statement: Best absorbency sits at an intermediate stiffness: the optimum uptake under load and retention occurred at G' of 150-200 Pa, with weaker gels collapsing and stiffer gels unable to swell.
candidate_laws.quote: The optimal absorbency herein occurred at an intermediate G' of 150–200 Pa for the 0.5% CA gel, which was strong enough to retain its shape but soft enough to swell significantly.
